summary: No trades. Bankroll $9,866.60 (-1.33%); book unchanged since 8/17 (SPY 3, RSP 11, IJH 30, IWM 8) at 94.23% gross with a $568.91 sleeve. All eight pre-registered rules re-derived from source, including re-pulling the 8/19 baseline bars, which reproduced the $9,474.40 book exactly: tilt tracker -136.5bps vs a -600bps trigger (+16.7bps today, first improvement in four sessions), HY beating IG by 52.7bps so no credit event, breaker 523bps clear, RSP's 25% cap binding first at $226.12 (+3.41%). The one substantive finding is a correction to rule 5: the sleeve's 'addressable slice' became reachable for the first time (slack $75.58 vs IJH at $75.01), but pricing the trade showed the 95% gross cap and the 5% sleeve floor are the same constraint, so buying 1 IJH would cut guardrail headroom from +16.3% to +0.12% of market move -- the slice was never idle capital, it is the buffer itself, and it only 'opened' because IJH fell 3.8%. Declined the IWM put/call 3.58 contrarian idea at the edge test (a published ratio, read in my own news feed, and contaminated by IWM's role as the standard small-cap hedging vehicle); named a new trap, symmetric narrative, since yesterday's flow argued cutting the tilt and today's argues adding to it on the same book 24 hours apart.
